coaching.headline: They took the map. We took the loss.
coaching.team: The enemy took every Fangtooth and Prime objective recorded, then dismantled our structures. Our winning skirmishes produced no quick objective return. We could win exchanges, but the enemy kept winning the map.

focus.title: Give the next fight a purpose
focus.action: Before the next objective contest, name the target, the player covering the approach, and the retreat condition. Check afterward whether those assignments happened, not just whether the team got kills.

perPlayer.16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Wukong brought strong damage and cleared enemy wards with sentry. Keep that denial. Before sweeping for a gank, call the target lane and confirm the laner can follow; before an objective, call the setup and whether the team is contesting or trading. Give the team a plan to respond to, not a fucking guessing game.
perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Revenant kept the farm and deaths under control, but hero damage fell below his usual output on the hero. A tidy score does not finish the carry job. Keep the discipline; in the next safe firing window, focus on landing the remaining shots before reloading, then reposition instead of forcing a dangerous finish.
perPlayer.a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Scarlett placed plenty of wards and kept deaths low, but recorded no objective damage. Before returning to lane near the next contest, cover a safe objective approach if a ward is available, then prepare the wave so a rotation costs less. Give the team a usable route; chasing a higher ward total is not the assignment.
perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Gideon had the team's most deaths, including one before the late structure losses. For the next contest, hold the escape until the threat is accounted for and agree on a retreat call with Steel before committing. Keep contributing damage, but do not let owning the recommended core become a fucking permission slip to overcommit.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Steel led mitigation and assists. Keep enabling the team. When the next gank or objective call comes, confirm whether Steel is engaging or holding control to peel, and coordinate the follow-up. Tainted Guard applies healing reduction to an enemy that basic-attacks its wearer; owning it does not mean every enemy being healed is covered.

matchup: Jungle against Yin, with ganks into Gadget, Crunch, and Murdock plus Mourn.
Crunch and Mourn finished with armor, so each gank target matters more than a popular list.
build: The Perforator and Deathstalker have a purpose against the armored front line.
Deathstalker needs repeated contact; do not assume its full stacked value in a brief gank.
eternal: Lotus gives random scaling, not a guaranteed defensive response.
Immaculate protects only while health stays high, so chip damage before the commit may remove it.
Keep it for healthy entries, not as a substitute for sustained durability.
augment: Masterful Mimicry supports the clone plan.
There is no basis here to declare another augment a proven upgrade.
crest: Nex fits finishing a gank, since its burst depends on recent hero damage.
It is not a generic defensive answer when committing into several enemies.
improvement: Keep the armor-answering tools when Crunch or Mourn is the reachable target.
If those targets cannot be hit safely long enough to stack Deathstalker, compare a survival slot before more damage.
Decide from the actual threat ending the entry, not the count of physical heroes.

matchup: Revenant and Steel faced Murdock and Mourn, with Crunch adding armor and sustain later.
Mourn's Warden's Faith directly reduces critical-strike damage, a reason to inspect target selection and armor answers.
build: Demolisher's armor penetration is relevant into Crunch and Mourn.
It does not erase Warden's Faith's separate critical-damage reduction.
Terminus cannot provide its shield without excess healing first.
eternal: Vermis needs consecutive attacks on one hero; target switches or reload gaps can limit it.
Serration and Melting Point have a plausible front-line purpose.
augment: Hellfire Blast's fourth shot ignores some bonus armor, fitting this armored enemy inventory.
It does not show fourth shots were missed, and its penetration does not simply add to Demolisher's.
crest: Use Pacifier's dash to preserve a safe firing opportunity as well as to finish.
A reset opportunity is not a reason to chase through the enemy team.
improvement: Keep Demolisher in the armor-focused plan.
If Mourn's healing is the problem, compare Tainted Rounds, trading a damage or sustain slot, not the armor answer.
Coordinate that purchase with Steel or Gideon; ownership alone does not guarantee coverage.

matchup: Crunch's Mutilator, Salvation, Draconum and armor make sustained trades and healing reduction relevant.
Gadget remained a magic-damage threat in team fights; physical armor alone does not answer the lineup.
build: Tainted Guard's armor and healing cut on attackers have a clear purpose against a trading Crunch.
Mutilator adds max-health damage; Terminus adds sustain.
eternal: Knell and Peal favor a prepared entry into an extended exchange.
Patina's shield needs damage-free time, so it is less dependable during constant chip damage.
augment: Volcaic Slam adds a delayed eruption and slow, pressuring Crunch if he stays in the area.
Its delayed hit is a condition, not guaranteed damage.
crest: Liberator's cleanse and shield matter when control prevents an exit or follow-up.
The record does not show what was cleansed or whether it was available at a death.
improvement: The existing Knell and anti-heal plan fits the Crunch matchup.
If repeated immobilization is the obstacle, compare Resonant Repair against Peal at draft: recovery and tenacity versus faster Rust.
Do not replace the whole build just because objective damage was low.

matchup: Gadget built long-range ability pressure with Soulbinder, Megacosm and Entropy.
Crunch's later armor and health change team-fight targets; lane and late-fight needs differ.
build: Azure Core, Combustion and Wraith Leggings are an offensive package, not a dedicated answer to Gadget.
The record does not show whether the Azure Core shield was ready when Gideon died.
eternal: Vesh, Tithe of Death and Phylactery work with the mana investment.
Phylactery's protection has a trigger and window; it does not prove the ultimate was safe to commit.
augment: Event Horizon's center hits add max-health damage, with a purpose against Crunch and Mourn's health.
Landing the center is essential; the feed cannot prove another augment would have performed better.
crest: Soulbearer complements the mana package with a planned defensive window.
It does not make enemy control irrelevant.
improvement: If the team cannot keep healing reduction on a reachable target, compare Tainted Scepter against a damage slot such as Wraith Leggings.
The trade is direct magical-damage application versus low-health finishing damage.
If Gadget's pressure is preventing contribution, prioritize a defensive comparison; the death count alone cannot decide which problem caused the loss.

matchup: Steel and Revenant faced Murdock and Mourn; Crunch and Yin added physical threats, Gadget ability pressure.
Build decisions should distinguish protecting Revenant from surviving an engage.
build: Xenia depends on ally proximity, and Dynamo rewards coordinated follow-up after an immobilize.
Tainted Guard only applies anti-heal to enemies that basic-attack Steel, not to everyone Mourn heals.
eternal: Krix's health also supports Xenia and Sanctification.
Festering Wounds is a meaningful draft alternative to Regenerative Tissue for applying anti-heal through immobilizing.
augment: Heavy Metal gives the armor purchases an offensive interaction too.
That synergy does not prove hits landed or justify ignoring Gadget's damage type.
crest: Sanctification shields Steel and nearby allies with tenacity, supporting a planned group commitment or peel.
improvement: At draft time, compare Festering Wounds with Regenerative Tissue if reliable healing reduction is Steel's job.
During the match, if Gadget is forcing Steel out, compare magical defense before another physical-only purchase.
Preserve Dynamo's follow-up and Xenia proximity; two Tainted Guards do not guarantee coverage on the chosen target.

coaching.lossReflection: The stronger alternative was to set up before the next objective. Send the nearby laner to prepare the wave and cover a safe approach, have Wukong communicate the gank or objective plan before sweeping, and confirm who can follow. If the approach is unsafe, call a reachable trade or defend together. Winning a skirmish is not a fucking shopping receipt for an objective; someone still has to call what is safely available.

threats: Chain-CC risk (3 hard-CC abilities, ~2.8s of lockdown): Gadget Security Gate (root 1s), Crunch Right Crunch (knockup 1.25s), Mourn Abduct (pull). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
Heal-stacking: Mourn. Anti-heal is mandatory against this comp — we brought 2 items of it.
Dive threat on our backline: Crunch. Assign peel for the carry and ward the flanks.
synergy: Little hard CC on our side — we can't force a pick. Play for poke/objectives and punish their cooldowns, don't flip coin-toss 5v5s.
We have sustain (Steel) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

lines: Lead story: Damage well above normal. 1,416 hero damage a minute, more than 82% of Gadget mid players this patch (35% of the team's). The damage came from Soulbinder, Tainted Scepter, Megacosm.
Tesla Dome at rank 3: 95s base, about 54.9s by the end (42% shorter) from 73 ability haste: Azure Core 10, Soulbinder 20, Tainted Scepter 10, Megacosm 10, Entropy 15, Soulbearer 8.
10 takedowns (6 kills, 4 assists) fed: Tainted Scepter (Malice), Field Data Accumulation (passive).
Gadget dealt 43,901 hero damage, 35% of their team's, with +395 magical power from items.
Soulbinder (item): Damage Heroes from afar with Abilities: Deal 8% bonus Damage. Activates at 1450+ Range.
Tainted Scepter (item): On Dealing Magical Damage: Reduce the Target's Healing by 45% for 4s.
Tainted Scepter (item): Once every second: Gain a stack of Malice. Stacks up to 15 times. Takedowns grant 15 stacks instantly. Hitting a Hero with Ability Damage will deal 1.5 (+1%) Damage per stack.
Megacosm (item): On dealing Ability Damage: Deal 2.5% of Target's Max Health as Damage over 3s. Additional applications refresh the duration.
Megacosm (item): On dealing Ability Damage to Heroes: Deal 6% of Target's Bonus Health as Damage over 3s.
Entropy (item): On dealing Ability Damage: Deal 3 (+3.5%) additional Damage. Each Ability can only trigger this effect once every 0.2s, per Target.
Aion (Eternal): Casting a spell grants 1 Mana Regeneration for 8s (stacks 5x). Spells also grant gold equal to 6% of damage dealt to Enemy Heroes.

Sustain: Azure Core: On going below 40% Health: Gain a 100 (+12%) Shield for 5s.; Soulbearer: Gain a 100 (+35) (+6%) Shield for 8s. Gain 20% Magical Lifesteal and 10% Movement Speed for 8s.; 2,221 healing recorded.
Toughness: +450 health; took 19,897 damage, mitigated 13,760, died 2 times.

(changes Sticky Mine, 4.6s cooldown with their haste) Field: 47.9% in 2728 games, 29% of picks, below the hero-role's 50.1%.

Loadout Eternal Aion: Each ability cast adds mana regen, and ability damage to heroes earns gold. Rewards landing Sticky Mine and Seek and Destroy on heroes often in lane. (game text: Casting a spell grants 1 Mana Regeneration for 8s (stacks 5x). Spells also grant gold equal to 6% of damage dealt to Enemy Heroes.) Field: 51.2% in 2467 games, 26% of picks, above the hero-role's 50.1%.

Loadout minor Sacrifice: Ability hits on heroes restore mana over time, more on kills. Keeps Gadget casting Sticky Mine and Seek and Destroy in long lanes. (game text: Damaging an Enemy Hero with an ability grants 3.5% Missing Mana regeneration over 5s. Hero kills regenerate 25% Missing Mana over 5s.) Field: 50% in 526 games, 21% of picks, level the hero-role's 50.1%.

Loadout minor Runic Focus: More magic power while Gadget's mana bar is high. Rewards poking from full mana instead of spending it all at once. (game text: Gain 0.2% increased Magical Power per 1% current Mana.) Field: 53.5% in 1126 games, 46% of picks, above the hero-role's 50.1%.

Loadout crest Soulbearer: Activate for a shield, healing off magic damage and a bit of speed. Use it as Tesla Dome starts so its long damage window heals Gadget. (game text: Anima:  Gain a 100 (+35) (+6%) Shield for 8s. Gain 20% Magical Lifesteal and 10% Movement Speed for 8s.) Field: 53.1% in 1352 games, 14% of picks, above the hero-role's 50.1%.

Stack (Every ability hit set off): 2 effects on one trigger: Megacosm, Entropy. Gadget has 4 damaging abilities (Seek and Destroy, Sticky Mine, Tesla Dome hit an area, so one cast sets them off on several heroes), and 73 ability haste brought them back 42% sooner: more casts, more triggers.
Countered? 1 of the 3 players Gadget killed built magical armor (Steel). We killed Gadget 2 times.
Copy it? Aion (Sacrifice + Runic Focus): 50.2% in 287 Gadget midlane games, level with the hero's 50.1%. A standard setup: what made it work was this game, not a secret build.

loadout.text: Sticky Mine's explosion radius is increased by 35%. Enhancing a Mine on an Enemy Hero grants 3 additional FDA stacks.

ability.name: Sticky Mine
ability.what: Launch a sticky mine that attaches to any Enemy Hero in its path, or any nearby Unit upon landing.

loadout.plain: Sticky Mine explodes over a wider area, and empowering one on a hero with a basic attack gives extra passive stacks, so Gadget gains magic power faster.

loadout.name: Aion
loadout.text: Casting a spell grants 1 Mana Regeneration for 8s (stacks 5x). Spells also grant gold equal to 6% of damage dealt to Enemy Heroes.
loadout.plain: Each ability cast adds mana regen, and ability damage to heroes earns gold. Rewards landing Sticky Mine and Seek and Destroy on heroes often in lane.

loadout.name: Sacrifice
loadout.text: Damaging an Enemy Hero with an ability grants 3.5% Missing Mana regeneration over 5s. Hero kills regenerate 25% Missing Mana over 5s.
loadout.plain: Ability hits on heroes restore mana over time, more on kills. Keeps Gadget casting Sticky Mine and Seek and Destroy in long lanes.

loadout.name: Runic Focus
loadout.text: Gain 0.2% increased Magical Power per 1% current Mana.
loadout.plain: More magic power while Gadget's mana bar is high. Rewards poking from full mana instead of spending it all at once.

loadout.name: Soulbearer

loadout.plain: Activate for a shield, healing off magic damage and a bit of speed. Use it as Tesla Dome starts so its long damage window heals Gadget.

lines: Lead story: Hard to kill. Never died in 31 minutes, fewer deaths than about 98% of Crunch offlane players this patch. The build added health and armor and healing off damage.
Re-Crunch at rank 3: 20s base, about 12.1s by the end (40% shorter) from 65 ability haste: Augmentation 20, Mutilator 15, Draconum 15, Mistmeadow Buckler 15.
6 takedowns (4 kills, 2 assists) fed: Draconum (Flow), Cannibalism (minor).
Their build heals off damage: anti-heal (the Tainted items) cuts it.
Crunch dealt 26,228 hero damage, 21% of their team's, with +262 physical power from items.
Augmentation (item): On Ability Cast: Empower your next Basic Attack within 4s. Deal (+90% Base Physical Power) Damage On-Hit.
Mutilator (item): On Successsful Basic Attacks: Deal 1% of their Max Health as Damage.
Draconum (item): On dealing damage to Heroes or Monsters: Gain 2% increased Healing for 5s. Stacks up to 10 times.
Mistmeadow Buckler (item): On taking Magical Damage: Consume Mistwood Guard charges. Block 1 Damage for each charge consumed. Can block up to 50% of the Damage received.
Judgement (crest): Deal 70 (+40%) Damage in an area around you. On Hero hit, Heal (+30%) (+8%). Subsequent Hero hits Heal for 50% effectiveness.
Combo Crunch (augment): Dealing damage with Cross Crunch grants 7.5% Total Attack Speed for 3s, stacking up to 4 times.

Sustain: 16% omnivamp; Salvation: On going below 30% Health: Gain a (+25%) Shield for 6s. Reduced to 50% Effectiveness for Ranged Heroes. Gain 10% Omnivamp for 6s.; Draconum: On dealing damage to Heroes or Monsters: Gain 2% increased Healing for 5s. Stacks up to 10 times.; Draconum: On Takedown: Restore (+120%)(+6%) Health.; Judgement: Deal 70 (+40%) Damage in an area around you. On Hero hit, Heal (+30%) (+8%). Subsequent Hero hits Heal for 50% effectiveness.; 26,038 healing recorded.
Toughness: +1000 health, +80 physical armor, +40 magical armor, +25% tenacity; took 48,799 damage, mitigated 56,914, died 0 times.

Loadout augment Combo Crunch: Each empowered punch after an ability stacks attack speed. Weave ability, punch, ability, punch to keep the stacks up and land more hits between casts. (game text: Dealing damage with Cross Crunch grants 7.5% Total Attack Speed for 3s, stacking up to 4 times.) (changes Cross Crunch) Field: 48.5% in 4163 games, 88% of picks, level the hero-role's 48.3%.

Loadout Eternal Krix: Generic tankiness: more max health, and you grow a little bigger. Nothing specific to Crunch's kit. (game text: Gain 5% (+1% per Level) increased Maximum Health, and bonus size equal to 0.5% of your Maximum Health.) Field: 51.6% in 161 games, 3% of picks, above the hero-role's 48.3%.

Loadout minor Regenerative Tissue: Heals you over time after a few seconds away from hero damage. Generic sustain between fights. (game text: After 8s without taking Hero damage, regenerate 0.2/0.4/0.7/1% Max Health per second at Levels 1/6/11/16.) Field: 56.1% in 57 games, 35% of picks, above the hero-role's 48.3%.

Loadout minor Cannibalism: Each takedown adds permanent max health. Generic tankiness that grows if you get kills. (game text: Takedowns permanently increase your Maximum Health by 25.) Field: 50% in 66 games, 41% of picks, above the hero-role's 48.3%.

Loadout crest Judgement: An area blast around you that heals per hero hit. Use it in the middle of a brawl when several enemies are around you. (game text: Thunder Cleaver:  Deal 70 (+40%) Damage in an area around you. On Hero hit, Heal (+30%) (+8%). Subsequent Hero hits Heal for 50% effectiveness.) Field: 47.7% in 2056 games, 43% of picks, level the hero-role's 48.3%.
Stack (Healing off the damage): 4 effects on one trigger: Mutilator, Salvation, Draconum, Judgement.
Stack (Every basic attack set off): 2 effects on one trigger: Augmentation, Mutilator.
Stack (Every takedown fed): 2 effects on one trigger: Draconum, Cannibalism. Each kill or assist made the next fight easier.
The Eternal was part of it: Krix (Regenerative Tissue + Cannibalism) sits on the same trigger as the items (every takedown fed), so the same hits paid out twice.
Countered? 1 of the 3 players Crunch killed built physical armor (Scarlett). Anti-heal on Scarlett, Steel. We killed Crunch 0 times.
Copy it? Krix: 51.6% in 161 Crunch offlane games, above the hero's 48.3%; this 3-item core: 51.8% in 365 games, above the 50.6% of that hero-role's cores. Proven this patch: worth copying.

card.lesson: Re-Crunch came back about every 12s instead of 20s by the end (40% shorter). Count it, and take fights while it is down.
